patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Squarespace and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Squarespace and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Squarespace only if your buying job matches “Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo ” rather than WooCommerce's shape. Choose WooCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPaymen” rather than Squarespace's shape. Workflow advantage: Squarespace leans checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce; WooCommerce leans catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Squarespace and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Squarespace is Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo annual (US 2026 tiles); platform transaction fees ; WooCommerce is Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPayments processing are separate TCO lines..
- Workflow coverage skew: Squarespace-leaning checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce vs WooCommerce-leaning catalog-management.
- Researched limits: Squarespace — Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume; WooCommerce — You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS.

Limitations — Squarespace: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume; Catalog and B2B depth trail commerce-first platforms; WooCommerce: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS; Extension sprawl can inflate TCO and maintenance.

Poor-fit cases: Squarespace is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume · WooCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS · Avoid Squarespace if you actually need WooCommerce's motion (Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
